headline: Friday: NBA (Bulls @ Celtics, Pistons @ Nets, Warriors @ Lakers), Friday night college football, and NHL. The WNBA Finals go to Game 7 on Saturday after Atlanta won Game 6.

record.label: Yesterday (Thu 10/29)
record.note: Rough night. The Packers won 27-19, so Panthers +3.5 lost, though the TNF Under hit (46). The Cavaliers lost by 3, the Kings lost by 12, North Texas won by only 7, and both the WNBA Under (149) and the Canadiens-Stars Under (7 goals) just missed. The board is down about 4 units overall.

notes: After a 2-9 day, today's card is small: one half-unit play, and everything else is a quarter unit.
No bet is a lock. 'Confidence' runs 1–5, and nothing on this board is above a 2 today.
Odds move. Skip any pick whose price is past the 'playable to' number in its reasoning.
Bet only what you can afford to lose. Help: 1-800-GAMBLER.

sections.label: Best of the Day
sections.slate: The strongest edge across today's card. Thursday these went 1-3. Only one pick today where two sources agree.

straight.reasoning: Action Network (via Yahoo) and SportsBettingDime both back Tulane. It's a buy-low spot after a six-turnover loss to UTSA, while Charlotte is coming off its best game of the year. Tulane beat Charlotte 27-0 and 34-3 the last two seasons. The line has moved from 13.5 to around 10 or lower, so shop for the best number. Skip at -10.5.

sections.slate: Friday college football: Charlotte @ Tulane and Dartmouth @ Harvard (4:00 PM PT), UCF @ Baylor (4:30), Sacramento State @ Kent State (7:30). Sources split on UCF-Baylor and the Kent State total, so we skip both. Full NFL slate Sunday.

straight.reasoning: Two sources agree, and Tulane has dominated this matchup the last two years. Skip at -10.5.
Harvard has scored 30+ in three straight, and Dartmouth has just three red-zone TDs all season. Action Network's pick. Quarter unit.

sections.slate: NBA Friday: Bulls @ Celtics and Pistons @ Nets (4:30 PM PT), Warriors @ Lakers (7:00), and more. One source per game today, so everything is a quarter unit. WNBA Finals Game 7 is Saturday in San Francisco; picks tomorrow.

straight.reasoning: Detroit is on its fourth game in six nights and without Jalen Duren (hamstring). Brooklyn has had two days off. 69% of tickets are on Detroit, but the line hasn't moved. TheSpread's top play.
Dimers' model gives Chicago a 57.7% chance to cover, its biggest NBA edge of the night. That's a lot of points. Quarter unit.
Dimers' model gives LA 62.2% against about 56% implied. The Lakers beat Golden State by 22 for us last week. Price is an estimate from a 56¢ market; playable to -140.
